notes: His question: how does being born and growing up work, how do couples come to have children, are there one-night stands, deadbeats. His hypothesis was that childhood is largely the adult code with different words on it. Traced at 2bdb7dcc; every claim below read from source and the reachability of each writer checked by looking at its callers.

HIS HYPOTHESIS IS RIGHT, and more right than expected. Situation eligibility, the adaptive selector, the resolution writer and the memory records are one path for both ages: availableLifeSituations calls formativeIntervalAt and delegates to the adult provider when it returns null (character-history.ts:1776-1803). life-content-92c.ts authors a five-year-old's stages and an adult's over the same machinery in one file. The age gate is one function, formativeIntervalAt (character-history.ts:1113-1147), which returns null at 18 and is what almost every other gate reads rather than comparing ages itself.

WHERE THEY REALLY DIFFER. Three things. The fallback bank of authored situations forks by band. Under 8 the player watches while the caregiver's temperament decides, which has no adult equivalent (childhood.ts:74-148). And a set of adult-only side systems is switched off wholesale by that same boolean: every contextual scene producer returns early below 18 (contextual-scene-producers.ts:116-118), as do the ordinary-life week and the campaign and office surfaces.

NOBODY IS EVER BORN IN A RUNNING GAME. A birth writer exists and is good: recordFamilyAddition (people-family.ts:153-414) records an event with both parents, then parent-child kinship, grandparents, siblings, child authority, household membership and knowledge records, all provenanced back to that event. Its only callers are people-family-plan.ts:408 and :418, which are only reached through proposeFamilyPlan, whose only callers are its own test. So the whole path is unreachable.

AND IT COULD NOT FIRE ANYWAY, because the family plan requires an active partnership and no partnership is ever created. createPartnership has one non-test caller, the partnership plan transition (character-history.ts:655), and the only thing that emits that transition is the ACS PUMS bridge (acs-pums-character-history.ts:618), whose only callers are tests. Twelve modules read activePartnershipsAt and in an ordinary game every one of them reads an empty list.

SO WHERE DO PEOPLE COME FROM. Every new person in a running world goes through one writer, createCharacterHistoryContextPerson(People) (character-history.ts:525-569), and arrives as a ready-made adult. Two sources feed it. Elections: every crossed election day runs congressional and gubernatorial turnover (time-work.ts:1632-1651), which mints successors and losing challengers (congress-turnover.ts:408, state-executive-turnover.ts:188) at an 85% House and 80% Senate incumbent return rate. And on demand: a classmate, a campaign opponent, a reporter, a chapter organizer, a legislative colleague and about a dozen others are created the first time a surface needs one. There is no in-migration and no arrival mechanic of any kind. The doubling from 555 to 1,053 in ten Kentucky years is the election machinery manufacturing candidates.

CASUAL RELATIONSHIPS: NOTHING. No dating, courtship, attraction, compatibility or encounter of any kind, and no state between strangers and a formal partnership. The only reachable romance is a private aim labelled 'Pursue a relationship' whose entire progress line is how many times you have been in touch (people-goals.ts:39, :521-548), and which has no completion path that ever creates a partnership.

A PARENT WHO LEAVES: NOTHING, and structurally it could not be modelled. recordPartnershipState, the only function that can end a partnership, has no non-test caller, and the plan vocabulary has no transition kind for it. recordChildAuthorityState is emitted in exactly one place, inside the generator that summarises a childhood that already happened, so parental authority is written once and never changes for any reason. At world generation a one-parent household draws unrecorded, nonresident or deceased (production-world.ts:695-724), but that variable is never persisted: a non-resident parent is expressed only as the absence of a household record, with nothing naming a cause and no conduct recorded. Death is the one family loss the game reacts to, and its scene is 18+ gated, so a child whose parent dies gets nothing.

CHILDREN PER HOUSEHOLD is a seeded four-way pick over one-parent, two-parents, two-parents, guardian, plus at most one sibling and only when the player answered that they share a home (production-world.ts:453-457, :538-563). Nothing about the parents' age, circumstances or history bears on it.

MEASURED, and it puts a number on the paragraph above. The divergence lane ran one Kentucky year and counted the arrivals with their ages: 556 people became 640. All 84 new people were aged 29 to 69, median 46, and not one was under 29, let alone a child. Every one is accounted for: 82 appear in world.legislative-seat-tenure events, minted by congressional turnover as successors and defeated challengers with a drawn name, a generated identity and a birth date computed backwards from a drawn age (living-world/congress-turnover.ts:391), and the other 2 in press.reporter-joined-outlet. None left over. So for that year the world grew 98% by elections and 2% by a screen needing somebody. One save, one year, one state: the shape is probably stable but the ten-year share is not measured, and nothing here rests on the exact split.

AND THAT IS ALSO WHY HALF THE WORLD HAS NO PARTY. A person minted as a defeated gubernatorial challenger is not a seated executive at world opening, not a chapter organizer, and not a consequence of party evolution — which are the only three things that ever write an affiliation. So every arrival by the route that supplies 98% of them arrives with no party, which is the 2% to 48% drift measured over ten years. See where-a-persons-politics-comes-from; the two records are one finding from two ends.
question: How should a life begin and grow up in this game? (1) Should people be born in a running world at all, and if so what should decide that a child is born — a couple deciding, or a household simply growing? The decision model already written asks one partner and lets the other answer from their own temperament, including 'not now'; is that the right shape? (2) Should a relationship exist before a child, given that no partnership is ever formed today? What should make two people become a couple: what draws them together, over how long, and what part does character play, consistent with the decision that conduct and personality drive relationships? (3) Should there be anything between strangers and a partnership — seeing someone, a short relationship, something that ends — and does that include a one-night stand, which the owner named specifically? (4) Should a parent be able to leave, to be absent, or to fail a child, and if so what should the child's record hold about it and what should later life read from it? Today a missing parent is only a missing record, with no cause and no conduct. (5) Should a population change by birth and death rather than by elections manufacturing candidates, and what should a town's population do over ten years? (6) Where should childhood differ from adult life beyond what it already does — the owner's reading is that they are mostly the same code, which is true; is that right, or should a child's world be made of different things rather than the same things with an age filter?

title: How a life begins, how a couple comes to have a child, and what growing up is made of
usableAnswer: A position on each of the six, in plain terms, worked against one example a player would recognize: a twenty-eight-year-old in a mid-sized town — how do they meet somebody, what makes that last or not, what makes a child happen, and what is written down if the other parent leaves. Rough shapes and ranges rather than exact numbers. Most of it lands on writers that already exist and are simply not called.
whyItMatters: This is the life half of the life-and-political simulation, and today nobody is born, nobody becomes a couple, nobody leaves, and the population grows because elections manufacture losing candidates. The owner's stated first priority is relationships, personality and long-life memory; a life with no beginning and no family formation has nowhere for any of that to attach. Almost everything needed is already built and uncalled, so the answer is worth more here than the code is.
